records.region: Soriano, northern tributary and lower Río San Salvador west of Dolores

records.region: Western Valle del Cauca, Colombia: selected junction-side Dagua valley through the forested lower river plain to the coastal estuarine wetland south of Buenaventura.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named receiving-river system; bounded confluence, river and tidal-arm names remain separate.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the selected connected river-and-coastal-receiving system. The field study identifies the Dagua at the selected junction-side opening and at Córdoba; independent imagery connects the intervening valley and downstream estuarine landscape. It does not establish one scalar name for every modern tidal arm, the exact naming boundary at the opening, or upstream portions outside the selection.
records.completion_scope: All stored parts and both terminal definitions were actually considered against the original photographic material. Ordinary connected canyon, alluvial and coastal-wetland correspondence is supported throughout. Clouds and channel generalization limit exact current-thread or bank claims, but leave no necessary receiving connection unresolved. Naming is representative, not formal registry acceptance or blanket reach naming.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected connected river-and-coastal-receiving system. scope_limits: The candidate is representative; names of individual tidal branches and exact local name limits remain unestablished.
This selection begins near a confluence and does not represent the entire natural Dagua source-to-mouth length.
Cloud, vegetation, generalized geometry and mosaic dates limit exact present channel/bank interpretation; ordinary corridor continuity is nevertheless supported.
The source and rendered sea-class endings occupy the same estuarine receiving setting but are not identical points or asserted surveyed outlets.
The CVC forest-plan403 remains an exact publication/project hold despite earlier lawful prose and successful unrelated sources.

records.region: Guápiles–Pococí lowlands and Tortuguero coastal lagoon corridor, Limón, Costa Rica
records.candidate_name_role: Representative downstream receiving-river system identity for the selected composite.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The upper Guápiles corridor and middle alluvial collector continue into the directly named Tortuguero receiver and its lower forest/lagoon setting. Exact name transitions, current fine channel position and a precise open coastal mouth remain outside the supported claim.

records.region: Argentine high Andes, Salina de Laguna Verde closed basin
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Río Salado supplies a bounded northern inflow identity, but no supported receiving-river name represents the selected downstream lake/salar chain. Salina de Laguna Verde is basin context and is not automatically promoted to a natural-river candidate.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Complete ordinary correspondence is established for the Argentine head-valley–river–lake–salar composite and its endorheic ending. Río Salado is bounded to the northern receiving river, with Laguna de la Salina/Tres Quebradas as its receiving lake. No supported river name represents the entire downstream selected composite, so the completed result is a null-name scope hold.
records.completion_scope: All18 parts, every join, the northern river/lake transition, connected saline floor, engineered-pond vicinity, lower basin narrowing, southern lake and separately retained source/render ending were read. No necessary receiver or terrain link remains unresolved. Exact wet threads, present exchange and current pond operation are outside this ordinary-geography finding.
records.supported_name_scope: Río Salado supplies a bounded northern inflow identity, but no supported receiving-river name represents the selected downstream lake/salar chain. Salina de Laguna Verde is basin context and is not automatically promoted to a natural-river candidate.

scope_limits: The whole selected composite has no supported representative natural-river name. Southern individual lake names remain unassigned in this finding.
Río Salado and the northern lake name are supported at bounded scope; they are not silently extended across the downstream salar and southern waterbody.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
